title: Fast Path SDK prototype labs – sketch
content:
Purpose and audience:

This is a lightweight, time-boxed sketch for an afternoon-to-2-day lab series aimed at product engineers, SDK maintainers, and Solutions Engs who need: fast confidence in Redwood SDK flows, clear failure modes, and concrete telemetry hooks to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.

Goals (short):
- Surface the most common friction points when integrating Redwood SDKs into a prototype app.
- Provide minimal reproducible labs that highlight streaming/function-calls, batching, caching, and telemetry.
- Produce 3 small example artifacts we can ship as interactive snippets in the dev docs.

Hypotheses to validate (each lab has acceptance criteria below):
- H1: A "hello" flow (auth -> simple chat) should be runnable in <10 minutes with copy-paste.
- H2: Streaming + function-calls are the largest source of developer confusion—an exercise that shows latency vs token cost will reduce support asks by 30%.
- H3: A live demo that toggles batching/cache will make trade-offs tangible and reduce misconfiguration incidents.

Timebox and audience paths:
- Path A (60–90m): Engineers who want a quick interactive demo.
- Path B (half-day): Engineers doing a proof-of-concept with telemetry.
- Path C (2 days): Solutions Eng + customer demo rehearsals with deterministic performance checks.

Module list (minimum viable):
1) M0 - Hello Drop-in (quick path)
   - Purpose: End-to-end minimal SDK flow (install, set key, one request streaming off).
   - Timebox: 15–30m.
   - Acceptance: User gets a streaming chat response, sees tokens and latency in console output.
   - Artifacts: small README + one-file example (JS and Python).

2) M1 - Streaming + Function Calls (behavioral lab)
   - Purpose: Demonstrate streaming with function/tool calls and graceful fallback when function schema mismatch occurs.
   - Timebox: 45–75m.
   - Acceptance: Demo app invokes a function via the SDK, collects partial tokens while function resolves, and recovers when function errors.
   - Observables: partial message timestamps, function latency, fallback route executed.

3) M2 - Embeddings -> Rerank + Memory (small app)
   - Purpose: Show embeddings generation, local index, reranking on recall queries, and a simple memory cache backed by KV.
   - Timebox: 60–120m.
   - Acceptance: Search latency under 200ms for 1k items (local sim), embeddings usage meter recorded.

4) M3 - Batching, KV prefix caching, and cost telemetry
   - Purpose: Contrast naive per-request tokens vs batched inference and prefix caching.
   - Timebox: 60–90m.
   - Acceptance: Batching reduces token usage by >= 25% in the sample workload; logs show per-token cost delta.

5) M4 - SDK observability and SLO checklist
   - Purpose: Instrument SDK calls to export traces, token counts, error classes, and model-variant fallbacks.
   - Timebox: 30–60m.
   - Acceptance: Reasonable out-of-the-box dashboards/metrics we can snapshot and include in docs.

Example quick commands (JS) for M0 - minimal copy/paste:

// install
// npm i @redwood-inference/sdk

const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

(async () => {
  const start = Date.now();
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-mini-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a 3-line haiku about coffee' }] });
  // print partial tokens as they arrive
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.text);
  }
  console.log('\nDone —', Date.now()-start, 'ms');
})();

Python minimal variant snippet:

# pip install redwood-inference
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-mini-1', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Summarize this page in 2 bullets'}])
print(resp.content)

Lab-run checklist (for whoever runs the lab with an audience):
- Pre-lab: ensure a redwood demo key and small model quota are provisioned.
- Local prerequisites documented (node/python v, pip/npm, env var, optional docker).
- Start with M0, verify streaming works before branching to other modules.
- For M1 add a broken function schema test to show recovery path.
- Capture logs for telemetry: request_id, model, token_count, latency_ms, error_code, batch_size.

Acceptance artifacts to ship to docs repo:
- 3 runnable snippets: hello.js, streaming-fn.js, batching-demo.py (single-file).
- Short slide (3–4 slides) showing measured token/latency tradeoffs.
- A tiny trace + metrics JSON export for sample dashboard screenshot.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Participant machine setup failures.
  Mitigation: Provide a cloud-based interactive runner (GitHub Codespaces snippet) and a smoke test script.
- Risk: Cost shock if attendees run many heavy-model requests.
  Mitigation: Set default to small models and enforce rate limits in demo keys.
- Risk: SDK surface mismatch across languages.
  Mitigation: Keep examples minimal and have one maintainer per language on call.

Open questions (to resolve in planning):
- Which small model variants should be default? redwood-mini-1 vs redwood-lite-1? pick one and keep consistent.
- Should the lab include a prebuilt Docker image for totally reproducible environment? fast follow: yes for customer demos.
- Where to host the interactive runner: GH Codespaces vs ephemeral Cloud VM? tradeoff: setup time vs cost.

Next steps (immediate):
- [Ava] draft the 3 example files and smoke-test locally (2 days).
- [Diego] prepare Codespaces template + a single-button run (3 days).
- [Li] sketch the telemetry dashboard and example panels (1 day).
- [Sofia] draft lab README and slide deck outline (1 day).

Notes to self / friction log (ideas to capture during run):
- Track the exact CLI errors new users hit during auth (most likely env var mistakes).
- Note where streaming chunk shapes differ between JS/Python.
- Collect exact language people use when describing batching — useful for docs copy.

Appendix: quick failure scenarios and one-line remediation
- Missing API key -> show command: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx
- Function call schema mismatch -> fallback to text-only response; show example diff and how to re-register schema.
- High token usage -> enable prefix caching or reduce model size.

End of sketch.

If team agrees, I want to run a pilot lab with Solutions Eng next week and iterate based on live notes.
